Buy a Chinese Passport on Telegram

A Chinese passport sold on Telegram is either a replica, a registered original, or a genuine document with your details typed in. Those three are priced differently and fail differently, and the advert rarely says which.

Issuing authority
the Exit and Entry Administration
Observed price band
900–3200 CNY
Typical delivery
3 to 21 days, tracked
Local name
huzhao
Document type
A passport is the travel document a state issues to its own nationals. It is the only document on this site that proves nationality rather than residence or entitlement.

buy chinese passport on telegram – the short version

If you want the short version, a Chinese passport bought through Telegram is only worth the money when three things line up. The stock has to match what the Exit and Entry Administration uses, the number has to follow that office format, and the seller has to survive a question about a feature a photocopier cannot copy.

Work through the rest of this page with the card in front of you if you can. The numbered process later on is the sequence to follow and the checks list is what to look for at each step.

Buy a Passport via Telegram: how the transaction works

Ask for the issue date and the issuing office before you ask the price. A seller working with the Exit and Entry Administration stock answers instantly. A reseller has to go and look, and that pause tells you where you sit in the chain.

If the seller wants to move to another app for payment, that is normal, but keep the conversation on Telegram. The chat is the only record that survives a disappearing account.

Who actually issues a Passport

In China the office behind the passport is the Exit and Entry Administration. The local name is huzhao. Use the local name in the chat and the seller immediately knows whether you have done any reading.

Register access varies. Some countries let you check a number online, some need the holder, some need a call. Ask the seller what route exists and expect a specific answer rather than a general one.

Replica or registered original

Replica and registered original are used interchangeably in adverts and they are not the same purchase. A replica is a print. It copies the layout and fails on UV, on substrate and on the number.

The failure modes are different too. A print fails the first UV torch. Stock fails the number. A registered original fails only if the entry has lapsed or the details do not match it.

What a fair price looks like

Observed adverts for a Chinese passport cluster between 900–3200 CNY. That is the range to hold in your head, and it is deliberately wide because it covers three different products.

There is a floor below which the maths stops working for the seller. Below roughly the bottom third of the band, nobody is buying stock, so nobody is selling you stock.

The buying process, step by step

Follow these in sequence and stop at the first one that fails.

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is the Exit and Entry Administration.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format the Exit and Entry Administration uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the 900–3200 CNY band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Checks that catch bad stock

These are the checks that separate a real Chinese passport from a good print. All of them are cheap to run and two are local to China.

  • Check the resident identity card for the eighteen digit number and its ISO seven thousand sixty four checksum.
  • Confirm the passport emblem printing and the machine-readable zone.
  • Check the number format against the published rule for the Exit and Entry Administration. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

Red flags that should end the conversation

These end a Chinese passport conversation for good.

  • A resident identity card whose eighteen digit number fails the checksum.
  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.

Frequently asked questions

What should a passport cost on Telegram?

Between 180 and 900 US dollars depending on whether you are buying a print, correct stock, or a number that resolves at the issuing office.

Is a Telegram passport genuine?

Usually not. Most adverts sell a replica or a registered original, and the two are priced very differently. Ask which one it is in writing.

How long does delivery take?

Adverts quote anything from same day to four weeks. A tracked number that moves inside 48 hours is the realistic standard.

Can a passport number be checked?

Only against the issuing office register or an airline check-in system. A seller who offers no route to a register check is selling a print.

What is the most common fake?

A colour photocopy of a real data page laminated into a blank cover with a plausible number typed in.

Before you pay

Print the checklist, run it in order and pay only at the end. That is the whole method for a Chinese passport.
